# v1.3.0-496: Telling twin windows apart by what they show

Builds on `v1.3.0-487`. That release recognised a window by the file or
folder it has open. This one covers windows that have none: two windows of
the same app, such as two Chrome windows on one profile, are now told
apart by what they show.

## Recognising windows

- Two windows of one app that nothing else separates are told apart by
  their address bar and tab names. Two Chrome windows with the same title
  now go back to their own places. It only ever breaks a tie: a window
  whose page or tabs changed since the save still finds its place.
- A File Explorer window with several tabs is recognised by the folder of
  the tab on top. Before, it could take whichever tab Windows listed first,
  and on Windows 11 a tabbed window wasn't recognised at all.
- Each Notepad window is recognised by the file in its tab on top.
- The window card has a new Content row showing the address, and the tab
  names when you hover it. Like the other rows, it can be set to require,
  prefer or ignore.

## Privacy

- The saved address keeps only what identifies the page. Query strings,
  fragments and any user name or password in the URL are left out, and so
  is anything that looks like typed text rather than an address.
- None of it leaves your machine. Bug reports don't include it.

## Fixes

- A profile edited by hand with an unexpected value in a window's content
  no longer stops the whole Load.

## Good to know

- Save or Re-capture a profile once to record the new details. Existing
  profiles load exactly as before until then.
- A capture or Load with two or more windows of one app open takes a
  little longer, 30 to 70 ms per window, while it reads what they show.
